title: Head-Movement Bounds During Recording
statement: Let $k,n\in\mathbb N$, let $x$ be a finite binary input, let $d$ be a configuration of the $(k+2)$-work-tape record machine, let $a$ be an action for a $k$-work-tape machine with states indexed by $\{0,\ldots,n\}$, and let $b$ be a Boolean record of width $4k+4$. Suppose $d$ starts in the record machine's initial state, the record tape contains $b$ at each of the next $4k+4$ cells from its head, and $b$ is the length-$4k+4$ prefix of the binary encoding of $a$. At every time $u\le 4k+5$, the first $k$ work-tape heads have moved from their initial positions by the action's prescribed displacements only when $u=4k+5$; the input head has moved according to $a$ only at that final time and otherwise remains fixed. Every work-tape head has displacement in absolute value at most $1$ on the first $k$ tapes and at most $4k+4$ on the final two tapes, and the input-head displacement is at most $1$. The record-tape head is at its initial position plus $\min(u,4k+4)$, and the summary-tape head remains at its initial position.
